summary:
Lunar Landing Site Navigator is an interactive decision-support web application designed for rapid evaluation and side-by-side comparison of lunar landing sites. Built with a FastAPI astronomy engine and a React telemetry dashboard, our solution integrates NASA JPL Horizons (DE441), NAIF SPICE (DE421), LOLA topography, NASA Moon Trek tiles, and LROC QuickMap deep-links.
It solves the challenge by evaluating any curated or custom lunar coordinate across a 4-Gate Feasibility Engine—assessing Solar Power Generation, Direct-to-Earth (DTE) Communication Windows, Terrain Slope, and +48h Launch Scrub Resilience. Users can scrub through a 29.5-day synodic cycle at 60fps, visualize real-time Sun and Earth trajectories across a 360° horizon sky-plot, and automatically discover optimal 30-day landing windows (GO / CAUTION / NO-GO).
By bridging complex orbital mechanics with a dual Mission Planner and Public Explorer interface, our tool accelerates mission trade-off analysis while making lunar engineering accessible to everyone.
details:
1. What It Does & How It Works

Lunar Landing Site Navigator is an end-to-end decision-support and data visualization web application that enables rapid evaluation and side-by-side comparison of lunar landing sites.

- Spatial Selection & Custom Coordinates: Users can select from 26 canonical lunar landing sites (including past Apollo missions, CLPS targets, international landers, and Artemis III South Pole candidates) or click anywhere on an interactive 2D NASA Moon Trek map to evaluate custom selenographic coordinates.

- High-Precision Ephemeris & Terrain Masking: The backend computes topocentric Azimuth and Elevation for the Sun and Earth across any user-selected date window (7d, 14d, or a full 29.53-day lunar synodic cycle) using NAIF SPICE (DE421) and cross-validates results against NASA JPL Horizons (DE441) to within 0.0001 degrees. It combines astronomical elevations with LOLA local horizon terrain profiles to determine true line-of-sight clearance.

- 4-Gate Feasibility Verdict Engine: For any site and landing timestamp, the system evaluates four critical mission gates—Solar Power Generation, Direct-to-Earth (DTE) Communication Visibility, Terrain Slope Safety, and +48h Launch Scrub Resilience—producing an instant GO, CAUTION, or NO-GO verdict alongside a composite viability score (0–100).

- Temporal Dynamics & Optimal Window Discovery: Users can scrub through time at 60fps across a 360-degree Horizon Panorama, Polar Sky-Dome, and Multi-Day Elevation Timeline, or trigger the automated Optimal Window Finder to scan a 30-day period and identify the top 3 safest landing windows.

2. Benefits & Expected Impact

- Rapid Trade-off Analysis for Mission Planners: Reduces preliminary landing site screening from hours of manual ephemeris querying to seconds via a side-by-side comparison matrix that ranks up to 6 candidate sites simultaneously.

- STEM Education & Public Accessibility: Features a built-in toggle between Mission Planner Mode (full engineering telemetry, configurable mission constraints, CSV/JSON export) and Public Explorer Mode (guided plain-language explanations illustrating why the Lunar South Pole features near-continuous grazing sunlight while the Earth wobbles in a fixed optical libration zone).

3. Tools, Languages & Software Stack

- Backend & Orbital Mechanics: Python 3, FastAPI, Uvicorn, Skyfield (DE421 SPICE kernels), jplephem, sgp4, NumPy, SciPy, HTTPX, and Pydantic.

- Frontend & Data Visualization: React 18, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Leaflet (integrated with NASA Moon Trek WMTS raster tiles), custom zero-dependency responsive SVG engines for the 360-degree Horizon Sky-Plot and 60fps Timeline Scrubber, and Lucide React.

- NASA Datasets & External Integrations: NASA JPL Horizons API (DE441), LRO LOLA Digital Elevation Models (LDEM), NASA Moon Trek WMTS tiles, and parameterized deep-links to ASU's LROC QuickMap.

- Development Environment: Antigravity IDE, Visual Studio Code, and Git/GitHub.

4. Creativity & Key Factors Considered

- Hybrid Ephemeris Architecture: Querying live JPL Horizons over the network for 700+ hourly steps can be slow or rate-limited. Our team engineered a hybrid architecture pairing ultra-fast local SPICE (DE421) calculations with live JPL Horizons (DE441) cross-validation, ensuring instant 60fps UI responsiveness with flight-grade accuracy.

- Launch Scrub Resilience (+48h Gate): Real rocket launches frequently slip. Unlike static calculators, our feasibility engine explicitly tests whether a landing site remains viable if the launch is delayed by 48 hours.

- Aerospace Telemetry UX: Designed with a high-contrast dark telemetry interface and strict monospace tabular-nums typography so rapidly changing angles and countdown timers never cause visual jitter during timeline playback.
